chapter: Early career, theaters and Cobb's Tea Room
title: Hustling for work and his wife's resentment (partly off the record)
summary: DeDroit talks about working lunch, dinner and night sessions while his wife complained of his absence; he asks that something personal be cut.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: He had a big tone. He played fine. And he played in comms for the dinner session. That was after, I must have migrated when he got in there because I used to own the place. I had the dinner session, the lunch session, the night session. I can show you programs where my name is on everything that's in the city, in the neighborhood. Well, I hustle. Many times my wife would talk about my daughter being sick and stuff. She'd say, you wouldn't know, you were never home. I said, no. I said, those $65 dresses would be nice, don't they? I'd be over in Biloxi and there's a dozen dresses over there. What am I going to do? I've got to get left. She has to have some amusement. And she had amusement. See? I couldn't let that stop me because music was my life. And she was my life. I was married to a fifth. You're going to take this? Well, it is. It is.
